title: Training with Confidence: Catching Silent Errors in Deep Learning Training with Automated Proactive Checks
problem: Silent errors during deep learning training (numerical instabilities, silent data corruption, incorrect hyperparameter application) go undetected, producing models with degraded accuracy
motivation: Silent training errors are critical for AI reliability; they corrupt models silently and are hard to debug. Detection requires automatic invariant inference
method: The system analyzes the training code to automatically determine what rules (invariants) should always hold true during training—for example, that numerical values stay within expected ranges or that data doesn't get corrupted. As training runs, it continuously monitors whether these rules are violated by tracking the actual numbers being computed and how data flows through the network. When it detects a violation, it alerts you before the faulty model completes training.
key_novelty: It automatically infers what should be true during training, then catches silent errors by checking those rules while training runs.
contributions: Automatic invariant inference for DL training code
Runtime error detection without manual invariant specification
Discovery of 6 unknown bugs in training libraries (TensorFlow, PyTorch)
Practical debugging tool for DL developers
hardware_target: Any hardware running deep learning frameworks
limitations: 2 real-world errors not detected; overhead during training not quantified; applicability to all DL frameworks not confirmed
